newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - June/July gas oil in contango.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - June/July gas oil in contango.

text.p: The Singapore forward gas oil swaps slipped into contango amid fears of prompt oversupply and hopes of renewed buying from China in July, traders said on Tuesday.
"The gas oil market is in contango because of the large prompt supplies in Singapore," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $24.75-$24.90 per barrel range, down about 10 cents from Monday, while July was quoted at $24.85-$24.95, up five cents, brokers said.
June traded earlier in the day at $24.82 and July traded at $24.875 per barrel, they said.
Traders said the weaker June prices were due to market perception that the support for the prompt physical market is waning in the face of a deluge of offers.
On Monday, eight sellers emerged to sell at least ten 150,000-barrel cargoes at around the $25.00 per barrel free-on-board Singapore mark, with one cargo traded at $24.80 per barrel.
The deal was struck for the lowest offer with other sellers holding out at just over this price against bids at $24.70-24.80 per barrel.
In addition to the lacklustre demand in Singapore, China is also coming under strong selling pressure as traders drop their prices to capture bigger market share.
Industry sources said that the traders who have bought record volumes in the Singapore physical market are now desperately trying to offload their cargoes in China.
As a result Chinese prices have fallen to just over $190.00 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis from about $200.00 about one month ago.
Traders said firmer July prices are partly due to market hope that Chinese demand will pick up then.
June fuel oil was last quoted down about 50 cents from Monday at $100.00/$101.00 per tonne, brokers said.
